entries.definition: Let X be a topological space. An open subset U⊆X is retrocompact in X if, for every quasi-compact open V⊆X, the intersection U∩V is quasi-compact. Equivalently, the inclusion U↪X is a quasi-compact map.

sources.title: Stacks Project — Definition 5.12.1(2)-(3)
sources.source_relevance: Directly checked primary source: quasi-compact map tests preimages of quasi-compact opens, and a subset is retrocompact exactly when its inclusion is quasi-compact; this gives the intersection formulation.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: U is open in X in this occurrence; retrocompactness of general subsets is also definable.
Quasi-compact is open-cover finite subcover without assuming Hausdorff.
U∩V is quasi-compact relative to subspace topology for each quasi-compact open V.

entries.definition: Let F be a field, let f∈F[T] be a nonzero polynomial, and let α belong to a field extension E/F. The element α is a repeated (multiple) root of f if (T−α)² divides f in E[T]; equivalently, f(α)=f′(α)=0.

sources.title: Stacks Project — Lemma 9.12.4 and proof
sources.source_relevance: Direct passage links a double linear factor and simultaneous vanishing of polynomial and derivative. Lemma states separability for irreducible polynomials; the proof's algebraic repeated-root criterion extends to arbitrary nonzero polynomials over a field.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: f is nonzero so individual root multiplicity is defined.
E is a field extension of F containing α; comparison occurs in E[T].
Formal derivative is used, including positive characteristic and possibly identically vanishing derivative.

entries.term: Euclidean metric on the real line
entries.context: Real analysis · usual distance on R
entries.definition: The usual Euclidean metric on the real line ℝ is d:ℝ×ℝ→[0,∞), defined by d(a,b)=|a−b| for every a,b∈ℝ.

sources.title: MathWorld — Distance, Euclidean space ℝ^n formula (3), restricted to n=1
sources.source_relevance: Directly checked Euclidean metric formula sqrt(sum_i|x_i-y_i|²); specializing n=1 gives |a−b|, with this specialization explicitly distinguished from verbatim source text.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: The ordinary real absolute value is available.
The codomain is [0,∞) with standard order.
The metric is on ℝ, not on an arbitrary ordered field without additional structure.

entries.definition: For n≥0, an n×n (0,1)-matrix, or binary square matrix, is an array A=(a_{ij})_{1≤i,j≤n} with every entry a_{ij}∈{0,1}. Its entries may be regarded as integers unless a different coefficient structure is explicitly specified.

sources.title: MathWorld — (0,1)-Matrix
sources.source_relevance: Directly checked the definition that each entry is zero or one, and the synonyms binary/logical matrix, with n×n as a square special case.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: Entries form a set {0,1}; matrix addition/multiplication requires a separately chosen ring or semiring.
For n=0 the empty 0×0 matrix can be included by convention.
No graph is assumed and no symmetry or diagonal restrictions are imposed.

entries.context: Set theory · symmetry axiom for binary relation
entries.definition: A binary relation R⊆S×S on a set S is symmetric if, for every x,y∈S, xRy implies yRx.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Definition
sources.source_relevance: Directly reviewed standard condition xRy⇒yRx, with no reflexivity or transitivity requirement.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: S may be empty.
R may be empty; symmetry is then vacuous.
No implicit reflexivity, antisymmetry, or transitivity assumptions.

entries.definition: For a mathematical proposition P, the Iverson bracket [P] is the numerical value 1 when P is true and 0 when P is false. This is a general indicator notation for the truth value of P.

sources.title: MathWorld — Iverson Bracket, displayed defining equation (1)
sources.source_relevance: Directly verified general statement-truth-value notation and its numeric 0/1 values.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: Values are ordinary integers 0 and 1, not an identification inside a zero ring.
The proposition has a determinate truth value in the ambient logic.
Floor-function brackets use a distinct convention and should be disambiguated by context.

entries.context: Set theory · antisymmetry axiom for binary relation
entries.definition: A binary relation R⊆S×S is antisymmetric if for all x,y∈S, the conjunction xRy and yRx implies x=y.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Definition
sources.source_relevance: Directly reviewed the mutual-relatedness implies equality criterion for antisymmetric relations, distinct from asymmetry.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: S may be empty and R may be empty.
Loops (x,x) are compatible with antisymmetry, unlike with asymmetry.
Comparability, reflexivity and transitivity are not required.

entries.context: Graph theory · open neighborhood of a vertex
entries.definition: For a simple loopless undirected graph G=(V,E) and a vertex v∈V, the open neighborhood N_G(v) is the set {u∈V:{u,v}∈E} of all vertices adjacent to v. It excludes v itself.

sources.title: MathWorld — Open Graph Neighborhood
sources.source_relevance: Directly verified the set of adjacent vertices excluding the base vertex and the distinction from the closed neighborhood.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: G is a simple undirected loopless graph.
v belongs to the vertex set, including isolated vertices whose neighborhood is empty.
The set excludes v; closed neighborhood differs and directed-graph variants are not implicitly included.

entries.context: General topology · initial topology from maps
entries.definition: Let X be a set and (f_i:X→Y_i)_{i∈I} be maps to topological spaces (Y_i,τ_i). The initial topology on X generated by these maps is the coarsest topology on X making every f_i continuous; a subbase is {f_i^{-1}(U):i∈I,U∈τ_i}.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Definition, family of maps and subbase
sources.source_relevance: Directly reviewed the coarsest-topology universal property and preimage subbase for general maps into topological spaces.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: No injectivity or jointly separating points required.
When I is empty, the initial topology is indiscrete {∅,X}.
If X is empty the indiscrete topology has only the empty set.

entries.context: Graph theory · finite walk in a simple graph
entries.definition: For a simple undirected graph G=(V,E) and u,v∈V, a finite walk from u to v is a sequence v_0=u,v_1,…,v_n=v for some n≥0 such that {v_{i−1},v_i}∈E for 1≤i≤n. Its length is n.

sources.title: MathWorld — Walk definition and simple-graph vertex-only description
sources.source_relevance: Directly checked the vertices/edges incidence definition and vertex-sequence specialization for simple graphs. Length-zero walk is retained as an explicit convention for matching a screened connectedness formulation.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: Graph is loopless simple undirected for vertex-sequence representation.
Vertices and edges may repeat; length zero is allowed for u=v.
Not a directed walk nor the strict graph-theoretic path definition.

entries.definition: A topological space X is sober if every nonempty irreducible closed subset Z⊆X has a unique generic point ξ∈Z, meaning cl_X({ξ})=Z.

sources.title: Stacks Project — Stacks Definition 5.8.6 items (1),(4)
sources.source_relevance: Directly checked primary definition of generic point and sober space; Stacks defines irreducible closed subsets using its nonempty irreducible convention.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: Irreducible closed sets are nonempty, as in the cited source.
Generic point is defined by closure of the singleton.
The empty topological space qualifies vacuously under the usual convention; no Hausdorff axiom required.

entries.definition: For a point x in a topological space X, a neighborhood basis (or fundamental system of neighborhoods) at x is a family B_x of neighborhoods of x such that every neighborhood N of x contains at least one B∈B_x.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Neighborhood bases and neighborhood systems
sources.source_relevance: Reputable mathematical source lead for neighborhood basis; exact full paragraph not independently certified here. Under general neighborhood convention basis members may be nonopen.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: Every basis member is a neighborhood in the general sense: contains an open set around x, not necessarily open itself.
Every neighborhood N contains some B from the basis.
If X is nonempty, a basis at x cannot be empty.

entries.context: Order theory · downward-closed subset of a poset
entries.definition: For a partially ordered set (P,≤), a subset A⊆P is a lower (downward-closed) set if whenever a∈A and p∈P with p≤a, then p∈A.

sources.title: Wikipedia — Definition of lower sets
sources.source_relevance: Directly checked order-theoretic downward-closure criterion; no ring or cut completeness assumptions.

entries.research_status: assistant-reviewed independent draft; not formally certified
assumptions: An empty set is lower by vacuity.
The underlying ordering is a partial order; the same predicate generalizes to preorders if typed separately.
No demand for directedness (order-theoretic ideals) or lack of maximal element (Dedekind cuts).

entries.context: Category theory · diagram of common-source arrows
entries.definition: In a category C, a span from A to D is a diagram A←B→D consisting of an object B and two morphisms B→A and B→D with common domain B. The object B is its apex.

sources.title: nLab — Span of morphisms, common-source arrows

assumptions: A,D,B are objects of a suitably founded category; no smallness is added absent source context.
No pushout existence assumption.
Arrow directions are B→A and B→D; the opposite is a cospan.

entries.context: Group theory · homomorphism in additive notation
entries.definition: For groups (A,+) and (B,+) written additively, a group homomorphism f:A→B is a function satisfying f(a+a′)=f(a)+f(a′) for every a,a′∈A. Consequently f(0_A)=0_B and f(−a)=−f(a).
